lis-001.voice: This work is so tedious. Find an easier job that pays better.
lis-001.situation: Restless dislike of your daily work, and the urge to switch to something easier.

lis-002.voice: Your leader is harsh and never shows anyone mercy.
lis-002.situation: Restlessness turning into criticism of the people in charge.

lis-003.voice: Where’s the payoff? I should be seeing results by now.
lis-003.situation: Impatience for spiritual fruit that hasn’t come yet.

lis-004.voice: The world looks more appealing than this.
lis-004.situation: Restlessness turning your heart back toward the world.

lis-005.voice: You don’t need to read Scripture. Some saints barely knew any.
lis-005.situation: Excusing yourself from reading and learning God’s word.

lis-006.voice: I feel a little unwell, so nothing’s worth doing.
lis-006.situation: A minor ailment draining all your motivation.

lis-007.voice: I miss my family. This restlessness is stronger than me.
lis-007.situation: Homesick and convinced you can’t beat the restlessness.

lis-008.voice: Skip the reading. Just ask God to teach you directly.
lis-008.situation: Avoiding Scripture with a spiritual-sounding excuse.

lis-009.voice: Why does God let me be tested like this, irritated by everyone?
lis-009.situation: Asking why God allows the trials that make you irritable and sad.

excerpt.from: that by them I may test Israel

lis-010.voice: I won’t cry. Tears won’t help.
lis-010.situation: A hardened heart that refuses the relief of tears.
lis-010.note: Evagrius calls tears a great remedy for restless, troubled nights.

lis-012.voice: There’s nothing left to hope for.

lis-014.voice: This way of life is too hard. No one could keep it up.
lis-014.situation: Hope fading as the life of faith looks unbearably hard.

lis-015.voice: Move somewhere else. Anywhere would be better.
lis-015.situation: The restless urge to move to a new place.

lis-016.voice: When I pray, everything feels dim and unsteady.
lis-016.situation: Restlessness clouding your mind’s clarity in prayer.
lis-016.note: Evagrius once asked John of Thebes where the light seen in prayer comes from. Only God’s grace can illumine the mind, John answered.

lis-017.voice: Even the angels have stepped away from me.
lis-017.situation: Feeling left alone and exposed to temptation.

lis-018.voice: You’ve waited long enough. God isn’t going to answer.
lis-018.situation: Losing patience while waiting for God’s mercy.

lis-019.situation: Doubting the value of tears in a time of struggle.

lis-020.note: Elsewhere Evagrius advises dividing the soul in two, one part comforting the other, using exactly this verse.

lis-021.voice: It’s fighting me all day long.
lis-021.situation: All-day restlessness and struggle, brought to God.

lis-022.voice: The anger and the cravings have finally gone quiet.
lis-022.situation: Thanksgiving when anger and desire let go of you.

lis-023.voice: They got promoted and became powerful. And me?
lis-023.situation: Restless envy when a peer or relative gets ahead.

lis-024.voice: Go visit someone. You need cheering up.
lis-024.situation: Escaping restlessness by looking for distraction in company.

lis-025.voice: Years and years of this miserable life stretch ahead.

lis-026.voice: This place is unhealthy. You need a new one.
lis-026.situation: Finding fault with where you live as an excuse to move.

lis-027.voice: My thoughts hound me and frighten me.
lis-027.situation: Persecuting, frightening thoughts, brought to God.

lis-028.voice: Lean back and nap. The work can wait.
lis-028.situation: Dodging work and drifting into sleep.

lis-029.voice: Skip the hard parts of obeying God.
lis-029.situation: Neglecting the effort that faithfulness takes.

lis-030.voice: There’s no love in this community. Nobody comforts anyone.
lis-030.situation: Complaining about others as an excuse to pull away.

lis-031.voice: This restlessness makes me so sad.
lis-031.situation: Saddened by a season of listlessness.

lis-032.voice: Old age, poverty and disease are all waiting for you.
lis-032.situation: Picturing a long, lonely, sick old age.

lis-033.voice: Somewhere else, life would be easier and you could help more people.
lis-033.situation: Imagining an easier, more fruitful life in another place.

lis-034.voice: Nobody sees what I’m going through.
lis-034.situation: Feeling that your struggle is invisible.

lis-035.voice: People in the world have it good. Lucky them.
lis-035.situation: Envying people whose lives revolve around the world.

lis-036.voice: I’m sick, and I’ve lost all will to keep going.

lis-037.voice: I’m so sluggish I can barely move.
lis-037.situation: Crushed under sloth and listlessness, crying out.

lis-038.voice: I’m worn out, weepy, and out of hope.
lis-038.situation: Exhausted and tearful after a long season of listlessness.

lis-039.voice: Take a break. Go home for a while.
lis-039.situation: Restlessness pushing you to take a long break from your commitments.

lis-040.voice: This life is all hardship and labor.
lis-040.situation: Focusing only on how hard the life of faith is.

lis-041.voice: You could be just as holy without all this commitment.
lis-041.situation: Thinking you can grow without the yoke of commitment.

lis-042.voice: This restlessness has grown too strong for me.
lis-042.situation: Overpowered by listlessness and crying out for mercy.

lis-043.voice: Go visit your father. It’s your duty.
lis-043.situation: Using family duty as an exit from your calling.
lis-043.note: Evagrius wrote for monks who had left home. The thought uses a real duty as a way out of a calling.

lis-044.voice: I want to go back to my family.
lis-044.situation: Longing to return to the relatives you left.

lis-045.voice: Surely Jesus doesn’t ask me to put him above my family.
lis-045.situation: Struggling with Christ’s call to love him above family.

lis-046.voice: Your family says you only turned to God because you failed.
lis-046.situation: Stung by relatives who question your motives for faith.

lis-047.voice: With all these troubles, why bother?

lis-049.voice: No one has suffered the way I’m suffering.
lis-049.situation: Sad, and forgetting what others like Paul endured.

lis-050.voice: Why be grateful for these people?
lis-050.situation: Unthankful for the community and mentors around you.

lis-051.voice: Suffering for Christ is just a burden.
lis-051.situation: Not seeing that suffering for Christ is a gift.

lis-052.voice: Give it up. Walk away from this path.
lis-052.situation: Wanting to abandon your path and your place.

lis-053.voice: Go back to the city and see everyone you love.
lis-053.situation: Longing for the city and your old life.

lis-054.voice: I’m being punished. That’s why I feel like this.
lis-054.situation: Believing your heaviness is a punishment.

lis-055.voice: The leaders here are cold. Why listen to them?
lis-055.situation: Fed up with your leaders and unwilling to follow them.

lis-056.voice: This heaviness has changed me for the worse.
lis-056.situation: Saddened by how long listlessness has lingered.

lis-057.voice: I keep bouncing from place to place and person to person.
lis-057.situation: Restlessly driven from place to place, worn out and humiliated.
